spans.text: Medicare Special Enrollment Periods (SEPs) provide opportunities to enroll in or change Medicare plans outside of the regular enrollment periods. Understanding SEPs can help you take advantage of these opportunities when life changes occur. SEPs are triggered by specific events, such as moving, losing other insurance coverage, or changes in your eligibility.

When you qualify for an SEP, you can enroll in a new Medicare Advantage or Part D plan, or switch between plans. This flexibility allows you to adjust your coverage based on changes in your health or financial situation.

One common SEP is triggered when you move out of your plan's service area. In this case, you can choose a new plan that serves your new location. Another common SEP occurs when you lose other insurance coverage, such as employer or union coverage. This allows you to enroll in Medicare without waiting for the regular enrollment periods.

Cost is a significant consideration during SEPs. Medicare Advantage and Part D plans can vary widely in premiums, deductibles, and copayments. By comparing different plans, you can find one that fits your budget and provides the coverage you need.

Network flexibility is also important. Medicare Advantage plans often have networks of preferred providers, which can change each year. During an SEP, you can review the networks of different plans to ensure your preferred doctors and hospitals are included.

Prescription drug coverage is another key factor. Each Part D plan has a formulary, or list of covered drugs, which can change annually. Reviewing the formularies of different plans during a SEP can help you ensure your medications are covered and find a plan that offers the best value.
